extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and media professionals interested in journalism, AI, and media-ethics
extracted.subtask_description: A news story reporting on a publisher's use of AI to draft articles, the resulting errors and corrections, and the outlet's editorial response and disclosure practices. Useful for understanding newsroom standards around AI use, accuracy, and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human editorial oversight of AI drafts
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors generated the outlines for the stories first, then expanded, added to and edited the AI drafts before publishing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI outputs should be used as drafts or outlines only; human editors must expand, add to, and edit AI-generated text before publication to ensure quality and accuracy. The article describes this as the workflow CNET used for the 77 stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full audit after errors discovered
rubrics_metrics.description: After one of the AI-assisted stories was cited, rightly, for factual errors, the CNET Money editorial team did a full audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an AI-assisted piece is found to contain errors, conduct a comprehensive audit of related AI-assisted content to identify additional required corrections and to classify issues as substantial or minor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections with editors' notes explaining changes
rubrics_metrics.description: The stories that have been corrected include an editors' note explaining what was changed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections should be publicly appended to affected stories and include an editors' note that states what was changed and why, giving readers context about the nature and extent of the error (e.g., substantial factual fix vs. minor language fix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear disclosure when AI was used to compile stories
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET has more clearly disclosed to readers which stories were compiled using the AI engine. The outlet took some heat for not making overtly clear that 'By CNET Money Staff' meant it was written using AI tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Newsrooms should explicitly indicate when content was compiled or substantially assisted by AI rather than relying on ambiguous bylines; disclosures should be clear enough to avoid reader confusion or criticism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pause AI deployment until editorial processes ensure safety
rubrics_metrics.description: We've paused and will restart using the AI tool when we feel confident the tool and our editorial processes will prevent both human and AI errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspend use of AI-generated content if existing editorial safeguards are insufficient; resume only after confidence that combined AI/tool and editorial workflows will prevent both machine and human errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid plagiarism / ensure originality of phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: One correction suggests the AI tool plagiarized. 'We've replaced phrases that were not entirely original,' according to the correction added to an article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check AI-generated text for non-original phrasing and potential plagiarism; replace or reword passages that are not sufficiently original and cite sources where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify factual and numerical accuracy (especially finance/math)
rubrics_metrics.description: An earlier version of this article suggested a saver would earn $10,300 after a year by depositing $10,000 into a savings account that earns 3% interest compounding annually. The article has been corrected to clarify that the saver would earn $300 on top of their $10,000 principal amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors must verify calculations, numerical claims, and financial advice coming from AI outputs; simple mathematical errors can produce wildly misleading advice and require prompt correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit use cases during testing (basic explainers, track share of output)
rubrics_metrics.description: The tool was used as part of a 'test' project for the CNET Money team 'to help editors create a set of basic explainers around financial services topics.' It amounted to about 1% of the total content published on CNET during the same period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When piloting AI in a newsroom, constrain scope to limited, low-risk formats (e.g., basic explainers), track the proportion of content produced with AI, and treat the program as an experiment subject to review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorize and fix both substantial and minor issues
rubrics_metrics.description: CNET identified additional stories that required correction, 'with a small number requiring substantial correction.' It also identified several other stories with 'minor issues such as incomplete company names, transposed numbers, or language that our senior editors viewed as vague.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality review should classify errors by severity (substantial vs minor) and address each appropriately—substantial errors need prominent correction and possibly retraction, while minor issues require targeted fixes and clarification of vague language.
